Hi Monica / Redwood team,

Thanks for sending over the DPA redlines. Legal has a couple of quick asks specifically around your subprocessor notification cadence and the objection window. Our procurement checklist requires:
- A 30-calendar-day notice for any new subprocessor additions;
- A clear objection process that results in either (a) mitigation plan, (b) segregation of data, or (c) a termination remedy if the subprocessor cannot be removed;
- Confirmation on how the DPA will be executed (DocuSign/AdobeSign) and whether you can send a single envelope per-customer that includes subprocessor addenda as they change.

We also saw the attached subprocessor list but would like an export we can use for our vendor risk system. Can you confirm timelines and provide the execution playbook?

Best,

Subject: Re: Redwood DPA: subprocessor notification & objection process

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear ask. Summary below and a proposed lightweight playbook so procurement/legal can map to your checklist.

1) Notification cadence
- We publish an updated subprocessor list monthly and will push an email notification to customers when a new subprocessor is added or an existing one materially changes.
- For high-risk subprocessor additions (e.g., new cloud provider, new analytics vendor with access to raw logging), we will send an advance notification with a 30-calendar-day objection window.

2) Objection process
- Customer raises objection by replying to the notification with details and impact.
- Redwood evaluates within 10 business days and proposes one of: mitigation plan, data segregation, or a transition plan off the affected subprocessor.
- If no acceptable mitigation exists, customer may terminate the impacted product-specific data processing for convenience with 30-day notice (we propose this as a narrow remedy limited to the impacted integration).

3) Execution & eSign workflow
- We run the master DPA in DocuSign. We can either: (A) create a new envelope per signature event (recommended for clean audit trail), or (B) maintain a master envelope and append subprocessor addenda via a signed addendum when material changes occur.
- For your setup we recommend option A for clarity; we will attach the full redlined DPA and the subprocessor list snapshot to each envelope.

4) Deliverables / timeline
- Today: attach current subprocessor spreadsheet (see attachment).
- By Wed 2/25: prepare DocuSign envelope for the final DPA (incorporating a 30-day objection window clause).
- Execution target: signatures by 3/03.

I've looped in Neha for legal confirmation and Dev to confirm we can snapshot lists per-envelope. Please let me know if the above deviates from your procurement requirements.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference

- We agree with per-signature DocuSign envelopes for an auditable trail; each envelope will reference the subprocessor-list snapshot date.
